description.p: The present invention relates to thrombin inhibitors that are useful as anticoagulants In particular, this invention relates to peptide derivatives having high antithrombotic activity and high oral bioavailabihty

Thrombosis is characterized by excessive blood clotting The condition plays a significant role in cardiovascular and related diseases, and thrombotic events underlie a significant proportion of the mortality and morbidity associated with cardiovascular disease Thrombosis can cause a range of disease states which are characterized by the location of the blood vessel in which the clot is formed
Thrombin is a trypsin-like seπne protease that plays a key role in the blood coagulation cascade by catalyzing the conversion of fibπnogen to insoluble fibrin This

enzyme also activates Factor V and Factor VIII for its own production and potently activates platelets as well Therefore, thrombin has long been recognized as a central regulator in thrombosis and hemostasis, and its inhibition has become a major therapeutic target in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases such as myocardial infarction, unstable angina, deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism

Indirect thrombin inhibitors such as hepaπn and warfarin (coumaπn) have been used as antithrombotic therapies with, however, several limitations Hepaπn demonstrates low bioavailabihty and is associated with side effects such as bleeding
problems, moreover, it is not able to inhibit clot-bound thrombin Warfarin is an effective oral anticoagulant but it has a narrow therapeutic window and also requires patient monitoring A natural protein inhibitor, hirudin, has been associated with bleeding complications

Most of the low molecular weight thrombin inhibitors are broadly based upon peptides or peptidomimetic templates which operate by a direct mechanism of action against the target enzyme Early examples are tπpeptidic aldehydes such as D-Phe- Pro-Arg-H and Me-D-Phe-Pro-Arg-H that have been reported to be effective thrombin inhibitors (Bajusz et al J Med Chem 1990, 33, 1729)

Recently, D-Phe-Pro-Agmatine and its derivatives have been described as thrombin inhibitors in US 4,346,078 and WO93/11152 (agmatine = 1-amιno-4- guanidinobutane) These compounds are different from the earlier tπpeptidic compounds in that the agimatine compounds lack a carbonyl moiety found in similar compounds containing an Arg side chain

More recently, certain tπpeptidic thrombin inhibitors in which 4- amidinobenzylamaine was incorporated at the P1 position in place of agmatine have been disclosed (WO 94/29336) These amidine-based compounds have been reported to possess good antithrombotic activity (WO 95/23609) However, this class of compounds has generally poor or low oral bioavailabihty
Certain thrombin inhibitors bearing the unique ammo acid D-diphenylalanine at

P3 position have been disclosed (WO 93/11152, US 5510369 WO 97/15190) These compounds have been reported to have higher potency against thrombin compared to the corresponding D-phenylalanine alalogs (J Med Chem 1992, 35, 3365, J Med Chem 1997, 40, 830) In addition, some of this class of compounds exhibited good oral
bioavailabihty (J Med Chem 1997, 40, 3687, J Med Chem 1997, 40, 3726)

In certain thrombin inhibitors and Factor Xa inhibitors, the amidinothiophene groups have been shown to be better para-benzamidine surrogates (WO 95/23609, WO98/24784 Bioorg Med Chem Lett 1998, 8 1683) In addition, 2, 5-thιophene and other 5-membered heterocyclic moieties have effectively served as a para-phenylene isostere in the inhibitors of other drug-targeting enzymes such as thymidylate synthase and glycinamide πobonuceotide formyltransferase (J Med Chem 1991 , 34, 1594, Cancer Research 1994, 54, 1021 , WO 97/41115)

Therefore there is a need in the art for thrombin inhibitors which have improved oral bioavailabihty and stabhhty as compared to those described supra We have found that the compounds of the present invention, as defined below, are potent inhibitors of thrombin in vitro and in vivo In particular, certain compounds of this invention exhibit high bioavailabihty after oral administration

such agents and their therapeutic use in treating diseases mediated by thrombin, such as myocardial infarction, unstable angina, deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, as well as other disease states associated with blood clotting and associated clotting factors
